title: fix: keep task retention from blocking the gateway
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Task-retention maintenance could block the Gateway event loop while waiting for SQLite write coordination. It now uses the existing read and write workers so unrelated Gateway work can continue.

## User Impact

Retention deadlines, cron-history limits, stored formats, and update behavior are unchanged. No operator migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The read worker prepares the selected task and fingerprint; the write worker revalidates that source and live authority inside the transaction. A compact commit receipt settles a lost reply without replaying the write. The publication owner reconciles indexes, activity, and flow effects before notifying observers, preserving newer owners and unknown outcomes. The superseded synchronous retention APIs and callers are removed.

## Evidence

The real coordinator-contention regression passes with this cutover and fails on the original synchronous path at the responsiveness assertion. Retained proof covers retention, publication, delivery, restore and replacement races, shutdown, and lost-result settlement. The full build, benchmark flow, production types, all 25 test-type graphs, script types and selected guards passed. Counts from the successive proof batches overlap and are not a unique-test total.

CI exposed an import cycle, variable shadowing, and fixture timestamp parity; these were corrected at their existing owners. The unchanged paging RPC reproduced its ordering failure before the fixture normalization fix; afterward it passed with its original 27-file cohort and 139 siblings.

The later asynchronous terminal writer exposed an unjoined restart-drain test. Its correction passed 20 full-file runs (188 cases each), three original 38-file cohorts (785 cases each), 59 completion/sweeper cases, and lint/format/owning test types on Linux/Node24.21. Neither bounded original-source probe reproduced that intermittent CI failure. The final size guard rejected the five-line addition to the oversized test file; main subsequently landed the canonical joined helper and extraction in #158344. This candidate adopts that existing version and removes the duplicate fixture edit. No size limit, assertion, or deadline was weakened.

Integration review also found that a committed cleanup stamp could lose its flow retry when managed cancellation returned an unfinished result. The retention owner now preserves that result and retains the existing retry obligation. The original module failed the new current-owner regression at the missing retry; the repaired row and all 128 cases across six owner/sibling files passed. The injected cancellation failure uses the in-memory command adapter; the separate retention, Gateway dispatch, and run-owner suites exercise native SQLite.

The subsequent main integration preserves #156919's final commit admissions for run-owner binding and task settlement alongside retention's ordered admission stages. Fresh focused review is clean, and the native Gateway dispatch and run-owner cases passed in the combined proof.

The earlier bacc head passed [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36190227569). The combined isolated run also passed lint and formatting, then stopped at main's two missing SDK projector calls; its later type-graph, size, and diff checks did not run. The published branch integrates the canonical #158520 repair while preserving all 199 pinned runtime-proof inputs. No overall success is claimed for that isolated run.

Fresh CI then found a newer SDK selection fixture still calling the retired synchronous deletion API. That fixture now uses the existing asynchronous retention command on the same store, preserving its held-read removal/replacement sequence and assertions. No production alias or new test seam was added. Managed review is clean. All 19 selection cases passed in the `agentic-plugin-sdk-hosted-2` group, and exact-head [CI for `dd00fe76e46b`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36215868576) succeeded across 173 jobs, including conditional skips.

Synthetic 64 KiB and 1 MiB profiles measured warm maintenance/publication timer gaps of 7–11 ms. Replies still use whole-object structured cloning; cold initialization was outside those probe windows, and peak process RSS includes fixtures, imports, and workers. These measurements establish neither deployed gains nor a per-message memory bound.

### Test cost

Each measurement selects one file per invocation. Node24.19 used a worker upper bound of two and reported one file; Node24.21 explicitly used one worker on a four-CPU Linux allocation. Wall time includes compiled-worker preparation, imports, and tests. The slower cases retain real database/worker or Gateway boundary coverage; replacing those paths with mocks would lose the contract this change protects. Retained CI output also reports 7.611 seconds summed across 49 registry-store cases, which is not file or job wall time.

The latest flow-effects measurement covers 47 cases and reuses the same lease's compilation caches after the focused negative/fixed probes. The SDK selection fixture migration adds no cases; its 19 existing cases passed in final-head CI. Their reported case times sum to 116 ms, which is not standalone file or job wall time.
